questions.prompt: An AKS backend needs a stable endpoint reachable from other workloads inside the cluster. Which Service type fits?
questions.explanation: ClusterIP serves the application through a stable cluster-internal address and DNS name.
options: ClusterIP
NodePort
LoadBalancer
ExternalName with a public hostname
questions.answer: ClusterIP

questions.prompt: A KQL report must correlate AppRequests and AppDependencies across the same Application Insights operation, and take only matching rows from both datasets. Which operation fits?
questions.explanation: An inner join matches operation identifiers and keeps rows with a counterpart. Filter relevant time windows first to limit input.
options: A union with no correlation field
A join on unrelated row timestamps only
Summarize both names alphabetically
An inner join on OperationId
questions.answer: An inner join on OperationId

questions.prompt: A long-running model API is becoming slow under concurrent requests. Which two measurements can guide a Container Apps HTTP scale threshold?
questions.explanation: Concurrency is the HTTP scale signal. Observed latency under load helps choose a target that preserves application responsiveness.
options: The count of inactive ACR tags
The maximum name length of the app
Request latency under increasing concurrency
Per-replica concurrent requests
answer: Per-replica concurrent requests
Request latency under increasing concurrency

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL knowledge base stores each document as many chunks. Which schema makes tenant filtering and finding a chunk's parent straightforward?
questions.explanation: Explicit identifiers preserve the source relationship, and tenant metadata supports constrained retrieval.
options: A chunk table with document_id, tenant_id, content, and an embedding column
One shared string containing every document and embedding
A single server-wide vector with no metadata
A table storing chunk titles only
questions.answer: A chunk table with document_id, tenant_id, content, and an embedding column

questions.prompt: A Service Bus message must be temporarily set aside and retrieved by the same workflow later. It should be skipped by normal receive. What should the workflow do?
questions.explanation: Deferred messages are excluded from regular receive and are retrieved explicitly using their sequence numbers.
options: Complete it and save just its destination
Abandon it and forget its identifier
Defer it and persist its sequence number
Set a low receive prefetch count
questions.answer: Defer it and persist its sequence number

questions.prompt: A Function App contains unrelated workloads that require different deployment lifecycles and process-level configurations. Which organization gives each workload an independent deployment boundary?
questions.explanation: A Function App acts as the unit of deployment and shared runtime configuration.
options: Deploy the workloads into separate Function Apps
Use one shared app setting for every trigger
Put every function in the same file
Use different route names within the same deployment package
questions.answer: Deploy the workloads into separate Function Apps

questions.prompt: A team wants evidence that a pgvector query is using the desired index and wants actual execution statistics on staging. What should it run?
questions.explanation: The execution plan reports actual row counts, operator timings, and buffer usage. ANALYZE executes the query.
options: VACUUM FULL during each API call
SELECT version()
CREATE TABLE AS SELECT on every request
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) with the representative query
questions.answer: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) with the representative query

questions.prompt: An AppRequests query should include only the last hour of rows. Which KQL predicate fits a datetime column named TimeGenerated?
questions.explanation: The where operator filters rows. ago(1h) returns the timestamp one hour before query time.
options: project TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
extend TimeGenerated = 1h
summarize TimeGenerated by ago(1h)
where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
questions.answer: where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)

questions.prompt: An inference API needs a different MODEL_NAME setting in staging and production with the same container image. Where should the value be configured for App Service?
questions.explanation: App Service supplies app settings as environment variables at runtime, so an image can be promoted without rebuilding for each environment.
options: A build argument baked into the image
An ACR tag annotation
An AKS ConfigMap in a separate cluster
App Service application settings for each environment
questions.answer: App Service application settings for each environment

questions.prompt: Put the steps for a Container Apps canary in order. Assume multiple revision mode is enabled.
questions.explanation: A ready revision can begin receiving a measured share of real traffic before promotion.
options: Wait until the new revision is ready
Route a small share of traffic to it
Increase the share after validating error and latency metrics
Deploy a new revision
answer: Deploy a new revision
Wait until the new revision is ready
Route a small share of traffic to it
Increase the share after validating error and latency metrics

questions.prompt: A Cosmos DB for NoSQL container uses /tenantId as its partition key. The API has both the document id and tenantId. Which read generally uses the fewest RUs?
questions.explanation: A point read addresses a single item directly using its id and partition key.
options: A point read specifying the id and partition key
A scan of every partition followed by local filtering
A vector search for the document id
A cross-partition SELECT filtering only on id
questions.answer: A point read specifying the id and partition key

questions.prompt: A team needs an Azure-managed Redis deployment for a new vector caching solution. Which service should it start with?
questions.explanation: Azure Managed Redis is the current managed Redis service in the AI-200 blueprint and supports Redis data and vector search features.
options: Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management
Azure Managed Redis
Azure SQL Database elastic pools
Azure Functions Premium
questions.answer: Azure Managed Redis

questions.prompt: A Python Function uses a Service Bus binding whose connection setting is named WorkflowBus. Where does the hosted function resolve binding configuration?
questions.explanation: Binding settings come from the deployed app configuration. Identity-based connections can use a documented group of settings.
options: Function app settings under the connection name or identity-based prefix
The Service Bus message Subject
The local Git configuration
The name of the Python virtual environment
questions.answer: Function app settings under the connection name or identity-based prefix

questions.prompt: An assistant retrieves Cosmos DB vectors for users in different tenants. What should the retrieval query enforce before using the results?
questions.explanation: Tenant restrictions must apply at retrieval time so the model never receives unauthorized chunks.
options: Filter on the authenticated tenant and scope to its partition where applicable
Trust the tenant string generated by the language model
Rank all tenants together and display the first result
Only increase the vector result limit
questions.answer: Filter on the authenticated tenant and scope to its partition where applicable

questions.prompt: A Container Apps job should run a short batch cleanup every night at a defined time. What trigger type fits?
questions.explanation: Scheduled jobs run at times defined by a cron expression.
options: HTTP ingress
Registry base-image change
Manual only
Schedule
questions.answer: Schedule

questions.prompt: A Service Bus worker performs an external payment. Choose two practices that together manage message redelivery safely.
questions.explanation: Durable idempotency protects the side effect and late completion preserves recoverability.
options: Commit the payment idempotently with a durable operation key
Disable every retry regardless of the error
Complete the message only after the payment outcome is safely recorded
Use a fresh operation key each time the same message is delivered
answer: Commit the payment idempotently with a durable operation key
Complete the message only after the payment outcome is safely recorded

questions.prompt: A sidecar-enabled Linux App Service app runs an OpenTelemetry collector listening on port 4318 in a sidecar. Which address should the main container use for OTLP over HTTP?
questions.explanation: App Service containers in the same app share a network namespace and can communicate over localhost on their respective ports.
options: http://localhost:4318
The ACR registry login URL on port 4318
A separate private endpoint assigned to the sidecar
The app’s public hostname on port 4318
questions.answer: http://localhost:4318

questions.prompt: An app uses the Azure Identity library locally and in Azure. Which credential class can use available developer credentials locally and managed identity in the hosted environment?
questions.explanation: DefaultAzureCredential tries an ordered set of credential sources that can include developer credentials and managed identity.
options: AzureKeyCredential
DefaultAzureCredential
BasicAuthenticationCredential
StorageSharedKeyCredential
questions.answer: DefaultAzureCredential

questions.prompt: A PostgreSQL table will store fixed 1536-dimensional float embeddings. Which column type fits pgvector?
questions.explanation: The vector type stores numeric embeddings. The dimension modifier enforces the expected vector length.
options: varchar(1536)
numeric(1536)
tsvector
vector(1536)
questions.answer: vector(1536)

questions.prompt: Application Insights telemetry is too expensive during heavy load. The team still wants representative trace data. Which setting should it evaluate?
questions.explanation: Sampling reduces retained telemetry volume. Verify that the chosen policy preserves the diagnostic coverage the workload needs.
options: Service Bus dead-letter TTL
The PostgreSQL extension name
Supported tracing sampling configuration
Key Vault network retention
questions.answer: Supported tracing sampling configuration

questions.prompt: A web API needs to accept inference work quickly and hand each request to one background worker. Which Azure Service Bus entity fits?
questions.explanation: A queue lets consumers compete for messages so one processes each delivery at a time.
options: A topic with an independent subscription for every worker instance
An Event Grid event type
A Function output binding without a destination
A queue with competing consumers
questions.answer: A queue with competing consumers

questions.prompt: An Event Grid event contains data.priority. You need to route only events with high priority. Which feature can evaluate that property?
questions.explanation: Advanced filters can evaluate payload fields using supported operators.
options: A subject suffix filter on the HTTP response
The Azure Functions timer schedule
An advanced event subscription filter on data.priority
The Service Bus DLQ description
questions.answer: An advanced event subscription filter on data.priority

questions.prompt: Several messages update the same customer record and should be processed in sequence per customer. Different customers can be processed independently. What Service Bus feature fits?
questions.explanation: Sessions group related messages and allow exclusive processing of a session while other sessions can run concurrently.
options: A single unordered queue with unlimited workers
Event Grid subject filters alone
A random session id for every message
Message sessions using customer id as SessionId
questions.answer: Message sessions using customer id as SessionId

questions.prompt: A Cosmos DB container receives many 429 responses during bursts. What should the application use when scheduling retries?
questions.explanation: A 429 indicates rate limiting. Respect the service-provided delay and review RU consumption and load distribution if throttling persists.
options: A new account key on every retry
Immediate retries with no wait
The service retry delay and bounded retry behavior
A full query scan after each 429
questions.answer: The service retry delay and bounded retry behavior

questions.prompt: Staging and production share an Azure App Configuration store. The same setting key needs different values per environment. What feature fits?
questions.explanation: The combination of key and label identifies a setting version within the store.
options: Different JSON indentation per environment
A different Git commit message
A separate Service Bus message session
Labels on the same key
questions.answer: Labels on the same key

questions.prompt: A batch job should send a reminder message that cannot be received until tomorrow. What Service Bus capability fits?
questions.explanation: Scheduled enqueueing makes the message available at a future time without an active waiting worker.
options: Scheduled message enqueueing
Deferral after the reminder is received
Immediate receive with a longer lock duration
Event Grid subject suffix filtering
questions.answer: Scheduled message enqueueing

questions.prompt: A pgvector cosine query orders by embedding <=> a parameter with LIMIT 10. Which HNSW operator class matches this query?
questions.explanation: The index operator class must match the query distance operator. vector_cosine_ops supports cosine distance.
options: vector_l2_ops
vector_cosine_ops
text_pattern_ops
vector_ip_ops
questions.answer: vector_cosine_ops

questions.prompt: A new Event Grid consumer must survive transient errors and preserve events after delivery attempts are exhausted. Which two configurations fit?
questions.explanation: Retries address temporary problems. A dead-letter destination retains events that remain undeliverable.
options: A dead-letter destination on the event subscription
A Service Bus session ID on every CloudEvent
A registry purge policy
A retry policy suitable for the subscriber
answer: A retry policy suitable for the subscriber
A dead-letter destination on the event subscription

questions.prompt: An app with registry access configured attempts to pull myacr.azurecr.io/worker:v7. It gets manifest unknown. Which check comes first?
questions.explanation: A manifest lookup can fail when the referenced repository or tag is absent. Check the exact image reference first.
options: Confirm that worker:v7 exists in that registry
Increase the app replica count
Increase the container port
Rotate the PostgreSQL password
questions.answer: Confirm that worker:v7 exists in that registry

questions.prompt: An alert should catch a regression in the slowest few percent of requests. Which metric is a better fit than average duration?
questions.explanation: A tail percentile highlights slow requests that can be hidden by a low average.
options: 95th percentile request duration
Minimum observed request duration
Total number of deployments
Number of distinct HTTP methods
questions.answer: 95th percentile request duration

questions.prompt: A Cosmos DB catalog writes a large JSON diagnostics subtree that the app never queries. Which indexing change can reduce write RU cost?
questions.explanation: Maintaining fewer index paths can reduce write costs. Keep indexes for paths used by application queries.
options: Exclude the unused subtree from the indexing policy
Replace every numeric property with a string
Increase read consistency to strong
Include every path and add unused composite indexes
questions.answer: Exclude the unused subtree from the indexing policy

questions.prompt: An Event Grid subscriber needs to recover events that could not be delivered within the retry policy. What should it configure?
questions.explanation: Event Grid can place undeliverable events in configured storage for later inspection and recovery.
options: A dead-letter storage destination for the event subscription
An App Configuration label for the endpoint
A Service Bus delivery lock on the webhook
A Cosmos DB query continuation token
questions.answer: A dead-letter storage destination for the event subscription

questions.prompt: Match each Functions element to its responsibility.
questions.explanation: Triggers start executions and output bindings publish outputs.
options: Start execution on a schedule
Write the function's output to a brokered destination
Start execution for a web request
answer: Start execution for a web request
Write the function's output to a brokered destination
Start execution on a schedule

questions.prompt: Which HTTP status code means an asynchronous inference request was accepted for processing? Type the three digits.
questions.explanation: HTTP 202 Accepted indicates that processing is expected to continue asynchronously.

questions.prompt: Your Container Apps API listens on port 8080. Ingress is enabled and configured to target port 80. What should you change while keeping the image?
questions.explanation: The target port must match the port on which the container listens. Public HTTP or HTTPS ports are handled separately by ingress.
options: Set the ingress target port to 8080
Set the replica count to two
Change the port on which clients connect to public ingress
Set the ingress target port to 443
questions.answer: Set the ingress target port to 8080

questions.prompt: Match each container release requirement to the best feature.
questions.explanation: Digests pin content, revisions route live traffic, and a timer trigger schedules builds.
options: Image digest
Multiple active Container Apps revisions
ACR Tasks timer trigger
answer: Image digest
Multiple active Container Apps revisions
ACR Tasks timer trigger

questions.prompt: An app loses files under its writable container layer after a new Pod replaces it. Which design preserves files across replacement on AKS?
questions.explanation: A supported persistent volume can outlive an individual Pod. emptyDir shares a Pod lifetime.
options: Use an emptyDir volume
Write to a different path inside the container layer
Set imagePullPolicy to Always
Use a PersistentVolumeClaim backed by suitable storage
questions.answer: Use a PersistentVolumeClaim backed by suitable storage

questions.prompt: A remote vector endpoint gets slower only after a release. Which analysis isolates whether the network dependency drives the regression?
questions.explanation: Dependency timing and end-to-end latency together show whether spending more time in a downstream call explains the change.
options: Measure the number of repository images only
Compare request counts without latency or dependency breakdown
Inspect Key Vault secret names only
Compare dependency span durations before and after the deployment alongside end-to-end request latency
questions.answer: Compare dependency span durations before and after the deployment alongside end-to-end request latency

questions.prompt: An AI feature needs a rapid rollout to users controlled by centrally managed settings. Which App Configuration feature fits?
questions.explanation: Feature flags let the application evaluate whether to enable functionality without rebuilding it.
options: Feature flags
Service Bus duplicate detection
Registry retention policies
Key Vault purge protection
questions.answer: Feature flags

questions.prompt: Match each Redis operation to the effect.
questions.explanation: SET EX attaches expiration, DEL invalidates, and TTL reports time remaining.
options: Inspect remaining expiration in seconds
Set a value with a 60-second TTL
Remove a cached value
answer: Set a value with a 60-second TTL
Remove a cached value
Inspect remaining expiration in seconds

questions.prompt: An approximate vector index is being tuned. Which two retrieval metrics should the team compare across configurations?
questions.explanation: Approximate indexing trades search quality against performance. Measure recall and latency together.
options: Query latency under representative load
The number of image tags in ACR only
Recall against exact search on representative queries
The number of App Configuration labels only
answer: Recall against exact search on representative queries
Query latency under representative load

questions.prompt: QA must access a specific Container Apps revision by its own stable test URL while public traffic remains on another revision. What should you assign?
questions.explanation: A revision label has a dedicated URL. A label can be moved to another revision as needed.
options: A KEDA polling interval
An ACR retention rule
A revision label
A Kubernetes cluster IP
questions.answer: A revision label

questions.prompt: An App Configuration key is a Key Vault reference. The app's provider already reads App Configuration. What else is needed when it resolves the reference?
questions.explanation: A Key Vault reference holds a pointer. Retrieving the referenced secret requires separate permission on the vault.
options: The Event Grid Contributor role
A new Cosmos DB partition
An identity authorized to read the referenced Key Vault secret
Only the App Configuration Data Reader role
questions.answer: An identity authorized to read the referenced Key Vault secret

questions.prompt: Match each Azure built-in role to its least-privilege task.
questions.explanation: These roles grant relevant data-plane permissions with narrower privileges than management or ownership roles.
options: Receive messages from a queue
Read key-values from an App Configuration store
Read a Key Vault secret value
answer: Read a Key Vault secret value
Read key-values from an App Configuration store
Receive messages from a queue

questions.prompt: A Cosmos DB SDK query returns a continuation token. The API needs to fetch the next page of the same query. What should it do?
questions.explanation: A continuation token records query progress and can resume pagination for the same query.
options: Increment the document id by one
Use the token as an account key
Restart the query in each physical partition
Resume the same query with that token and compatible options
questions.answer: Resume the same query with that token and compatible options

questions.prompt: KQL must display all recent requests, including ones that have no recorded dependency calls. Which join flavor preserves requests when they are on the left side?
questions.explanation: A leftouter join keeps all records from the left side and enriches them with right-side matches where available.
options: leftouter
rightsemi
leftanti
inner
questions.answer: leftouter

questions.prompt: A Container Apps revision is healthy, but requests to a downstream API fail. The team needs to test DNS and HTTP connectivity from the app's running environment. What is the most direct diagnostic?
questions.explanation: Testing from the affected workload exercises that environment's DNS, routing, and outbound connectivity.
options: Open a console to the running container and test name resolution and the endpoint
Increase the public traffic weight
Run the same request from a developer laptop only
Inspect only the ACR tag list
questions.answer: Open a console to the running container and test name resolution and the endpoint

questions.prompt: Order the KQL operations needed to chart failures by minute in a filtered time range.
questions.explanation: Select and filter relevant telemetry before aggregating to a chartable time series.
options: Filter to the desired time range and failed requests
Summarize counts into one-minute bins
Render the result as a time chart
Start with the request telemetry table
answer: Start with the request telemetry table
Filter to the desired time range and failed requests
Summarize counts into one-minute bins
Render the result as a time chart

questions.prompt: Put successful PeekLock processing in order.
questions.explanation: Settle a success after the durable result exists, so an interruption before settlement can be handled safely.
options: Commit the business result idempotently
Complete the message
Validate the payload and operation identifier
Receive and lock the message
answer: Receive and lock the message
Validate the payload and operation identifier
Commit the business result idempotently
Complete the message

questions.prompt: A function writes a Service Bus message and needs to receive structured details from an unsuccessful send within its own code. Which approach gives direct control over the send operation?
questions.explanation: The SDK gives the function explicit send calls and lets it handle exceptions at that point in the code.
options: Use an output binding as the only send mechanism
Use the Service Bus SDK client in the function
Enable Function App log streaming only
Move the send to a timer trigger with no client
questions.answer: Use the Service Bus SDK client in the function

questions.prompt: An HTTP-triggered Azure Function needs to accept a JSON inference request. Which element starts the execution?
questions.explanation: A trigger invokes the function in response to a request. An output binding sends a value to another service.
options: A deployment slot
The HTTP trigger
A Service Bus output binding
An application setting
questions.answer: The HTTP trigger

questions.prompt: Put the steps for a coordinated credential rotation in order. The old and new credentials can overlap.
questions.explanation: Overlapping credentials and confirming new authentication before revocation reduce downtime.
options: Refresh the app or roll it out with access to the new version
Verify successful calls using the new credential
Revoke the previous credential
Create the replacement credential and publish a new Key Vault secret version
answer: Create the replacement credential and publish a new Key Vault secret version
Refresh the app or roll it out with access to the new version
Verify successful calls using the new credential
Revoke the previous credential

questions.prompt: An app must read configuration values and secret values without storing cloud credentials. Which two data roles grant a managed identity the minimum relevant read permissions?
questions.explanation: The identity requires separate read permission for each service's data plane. Scope each grant to required resources.
options: Key Vault Secrets User on the vault or appropriate secret scope
App Configuration Data Reader on the store
Key Vault Secrets Officer on the entire resource group
Owner on the subscription
answer: App Configuration Data Reader on the store
Key Vault Secrets User on the vault or appropriate secret scope

questions.prompt: An AKS release needs to update the image through source-controlled manifests. Put the release steps in order.
questions.explanation: The image must exist before it is deployed. Rollout checks happen after Kubernetes receives the new template.
options: Observe rollout status and readiness
Build and publish the new image
Update the Deployment manifest to reference that image
Apply the updated manifest
answer: Build and publish the new image
Update the Deployment manifest to reference that image
Apply the updated manifest
Observe rollout status and readiness

questions.prompt: A Cosmos DB container receives new and updated product documents. A worker should refresh embeddings based on document changes without repeatedly scanning the whole container. What should it consume?
questions.explanation: The change feed exposes item changes incrementally so the worker can process relevant updates.
options: The account activity log
The Cosmos DB account key history
The vector index configuration
The Cosmos DB change feed
questions.answer: The Cosmos DB change feed

questions.prompt: A RAG assistant needs to cite the source for each retrieved chunk. What data must be preserved through retrieval?
questions.explanation: Citations require stable provenance from chunks back to source documents. A similarity score cannot identify that source.
options: Document identifiers or URIs together with chunk provenance
Only the final generated answer
Only the cosine score
Only the timestamp for the API request
questions.answer: Document identifiers or URIs together with chunk provenance

questions.prompt: Two apps run in the same Container Apps environment. Only the front end should invoke the backend over HTTP. Which backend ingress exposure avoids public access?
questions.explanation: Internal ingress allows access from within the Container Apps environment while keeping the backend off public ingress.
options: External ingress with a 100 percent revision weight
External ingress with a startup probe
No ingress and an ACR Tasks trigger
Internal ingress
questions.answer: Internal ingress

questions.prompt: A compliance policy requires that deleted Key Vault secrets cannot be permanently purged during the retention period. Which protection fits?
questions.explanation: Purge protection prevents permanent deletion during retention, including by principals with purge privileges.
options: The Key Vault Reader role alone
Purge protection
A Redis TTL
An App Configuration label
questions.answer: Purge protection

questions.prompt: An evaluation compares exact and approximate PostgreSQL retrieval. User-visible latency is acceptable, but the approximate search returns too few matches under a department filter. What should the team measure next?
questions.explanation: Approximate index filtering can reduce returned matches. Evaluate recall and candidate effort using the actual filtered workload.

caseStudy.title: AtlasDocs
caseStudy.background: AtlasDocs runs document retrieval in Azure Database for PostgreSQL with pgvector. Callers can search only their department. An Azure Managed Redis cache stores generated summaries, while the source database remains authoritative for content updates.

options: Only total documents across all departments
Recall and result counts with representative filters while tuning candidate search settings
Embedding bytes per Git commit
Only the number of API replicas
questions.answer: Recall and result counts with representative filters while tuning candidate search settings

questions.prompt: The source database remains authoritative. A cached summary occasionally persists after a product update. The team wants to reduce staleness during normal operation and bound it if invalidation fails. What should it combine?
questions.explanation: Event-driven invalidation removes stale values promptly, and a TTL bounds how long a missed invalidation can affect readers.

caseStudy.title: AtlasDocs
caseStudy.background: AtlasDocs runs document retrieval in Azure Database for PostgreSQL with pgvector. Callers can search only their department. An Azure Managed Redis cache stores generated summaries, while the source database remains authoritative for content updates.

options: Persist all Redis keys permanently
Set a longer TTL and skip invalidations
Invalidate on successful writes and set a finite TTL
Generate different cache keys on each read without expiration
questions.answer: Invalidate on successful writes and set a finite TTL
